entities.name: Early gut microbiome and temperament
observations: Human studies from infancy through preschool report associations between gut microbial diversity or community composition and measured temperament dimensions, including surgency, negative emotionality and fear reactivity.
Associations vary by age, sex, temperament domain and cohort; taxa and effect directions are inconsistent, and one prospective cohort's cluster associations did not survive FDR correction.
Evidence is observational and often small-to-moderate, frequently based on caregiver reports and 16S sequencing; it does not establish causality or a reproducible microbial signature.
